description: A circuit is the venue of a race; the race record carries no independent venue information and is meaningless without its circuit.
A season is composed of the races of one championship year.
A race is composed of its result entries; an entry cannot exist without the race it belongs to.
A driver's career record is composed of result entries, one per race entered.
A constructor's record is composed of the result entries of its cars, one per driver per race.
A race is composed of the individual lap records set during it.
A driver's lap records are composed into their per-race pacing profile.
A race weekend is composed of its qualifying results, recorded for the drivers that took part.
A driver's qualifying record is composed of one qualifying row per race weekend.
A constructor's qualifying record is the collection of qualifying rows of its cars.
The constructor-level scoring of a race is composed of one row per constructor that took part.
A constructor's per-race scoring history is the composition of its constructor race results, including scoreless races.
A driver's championship progression is the composition of their cumulative standing snapshots.
A constructor's championship progression is the composition of its cumulative standing snapshots.
Every result entry carries exactly one outcome status explaining whether and why the driver completed the race.

connection_condition: the finisher category selects the single status value 'Finished' from the status vocabulary
description: Finisher status is a restricted kind of race status: its value set is the subset of status values that denote a classified finish.

connection_condition: the champion is a row of the drivers table identified through the standings
description: A season champion is a specific driver: the one who holds championship position 1 after the final round of a season.
Each driver carries exactly one sporting nationality expressed as a country adjective.
Each constructor carries exactly one sporting nationality expressed with the same country-adjective vocabulary used for drivers.

connection_condition: results.driverId and results.constructorId appear on the same result entry; qualifying also carries both identifiers
description: Drivers compete for constructors; the pairing is recorded per result entry rather than as a direct team membership reference.
Each circuit carries the country in which it is physically located.
Each circuit carries a latitude and longitude pair describing its geographic position.
Each circuit carries the locality in which it is situated.
Each circuit carries a short stable reference slug alongside its full name.
Each driver carries a short stable reference slug alongside the personal name.
Drivers of the modern era carry a three-letter abbreviated code in addition to the reference slug.
Each constructor carries a short stable reference slug alongside its team name.

connection_condition: constructors.url, circuits.url, races.url and seasons.url all hold reference links
description: Entities in the schema carry an external reference link; for a constructor it is the team website reference.

connection_condition: drivers.nationality and constructors.nationality both store country adjectives such as 'Japanese', 'German', 'French', 'Dutch'
description: Driver and constructor nationality are the same business concept expressed over the same value domain in two different tables, so a nationality filter learned on one side carries to the other.

connection_condition: results.points and constructorResults.points hold per-race scores; driverStandings.points and constructorStandings.points hold the running totals of the same concept
description: Per-race points and standing points express the same business concept of championship points at two different grains; the standing value is the running total of the per-race values.

connection_condition: results.fastestLapTime holds the quickest lap of a driver in a race; the same value is the minimum of lapTimes.milliseconds for that driver and race
description: The precomputed fastest lap time and the minimum of the per-lap times measure the same thing at different granularity, so either representation can ground a fastest-lap question.
The driver full name is derived by joining the forename and the surname.

connection_condition: drivers.dob compared with a reference date, or simply the year component of dob for birth-year questions
description: Driver age is derived from the date of birth; the oldest driver is the one with the earliest birth date and the youngest the one with the latest.

connection_condition: a result entry counts as completed exactly when its finish time is present
description: Race completion is derived from the presence of a race finish time on the result entry.

connection_condition: count of completed entries divided by the count of all entries in the same population
description: The race completion rate is derived as the share of completed entries within the population of interest.

connection_condition: the entry with classification order 1, equivalently the only entry whose finish time is an absolute race duration
description: The race winner is derived from the result entries of the race as the entry classified first.

connection_condition: count of races in which the driver or constructor is the winner, or the cumulative wins counter in the standings tables
description: Wins are derived by counting the races won, which the standings tables also expose as a running counter.

connection_condition: the row with championship position 1 at the highest round of the season; the constructor analogue uses constructorStandings
description: The season champion is derived from the standings as the leader after the final round of the season.

connection_condition: minimum of lapTimes.milliseconds for a driver within one race
description: A driver's fastest lap time in a race is derived as the minimum of that driver's lap times in the race.

connection_condition: the lap ordinal at which the minimum lap time of the driver in the race occurs
description: The fastest lap number is derived from the fastest lap time as the lap on which that minimum was set.

connection_condition: ordering of the fastest lap times of all drivers within one race
description: The fastest lap rank is derived by ordering the fastest lap times of a race; rank 1 identifies the driver with the quickest lap.

connection_condition: running total of per-race points across the races of a season up to and including the current race
description: Standing points are derived as the cumulative sum of per-race points across a season.

connection_condition: dense ranking of the cumulative standing points within a race snapshot
description: The championship position is derived by ranking the cumulative standing points of the competitors at that point of the season.
